source_title: Effects of Cultivar, Nitrogen Rate and Harvest Time on the Content of Carbohydrates and Protein in the Biomass of Perennial Ryegrass
geography: Agricultural Experiment Station, Tomaszkowo, north-eastern Poland (53°42′40.8″ N, 20°26′04.7″ E)
material_scope: Cultivated perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne L.), cultivars Bajka and Baronka; not roadside grass.
experimental_conditions: Split-plot field experiment with four replications; nitrogen rates 0, 120, and 240 kg N/ha; harvest-time groups 08:00-10:00, 12:00-14:00, and 16:00-18:00; four sequential cuts. Tables report marginal means by factor group, not all joint factor combinations.
source_location: Tables 2 (WSC), 3 (crude protein), and 4 (WSC:CP ratio); Materials and Methods §§2.1-2.3. Publisher HTML tables.
measurement_basis: WSC and crude protein: g/kg dry matter; WSC:CP ratio: kg WSC per kg CP.
uncertainty: The cited tables report marginal means and significance groups but no SD or standard error; do not infer a probability distribution.
applicability: Reference-only feed-characterization evidence for perennial ryegrass. It can inform cross-context comparisons of cultivar, nitrogen treatment, harvest time, and cut effects but cannot populate GreenHub roadside-grass defaults or protein-speciation pools.
conversion_and_scaling: Values transcribed as printed; no conversion, scaling, or cross-study transfer applied.
metadata_gaps: No raw replicate data or uncertainty spread is reported in Tables 2-4.
The tables are marginal means; joint cultivar × nitrogen × harvest-time × cut combinations cannot be reconstructed.
The cultivated ryegrass field material is not a Dutch roadside-grass sample.
Crude protein does not identify true protein, soluble/insoluble partition, amino-acid profile, or extractable protein.
Water-soluble carbohydrates are aggregate measurements and are not resolved into individual sugars.
